guideTitle: 6 Best Bath Lifts for Tubs in 2026
metaTitle: Best Bath Lifts for Tubs in 2026
metaDescription: Six bath lifts compared by lifting range, tub-bottom clearance, recline, weight rating and waterproofing, from a reclining electric chair to an air cushion.
introParagraphs: A bath lift answers a different question from a transfer bench. A bench helps you get over the tub wall. A bath lift helps you get down to the bottom of the tub and back up again, which is the part many people with weak legs or sore knees cannot do at all. A powered seat sits on the tub floor, lowers on a button press until you are close to the bottom, and raises you back to tub-edge height when the bath is over.

The six picks here are all powered and waterproof, and they take four different approaches. The Drive Medical Bellavita lowers to 2.6 inches from the tub bottom and reclines 50 degrees, the Platinum Health Tranquilo reaches 21.5 inches and has a rotating seat, the PERLECARE and VOCIC AX10 are foldable electric chairs with IP68 ratings, and the SuperHandy offers both a folding aluminum lift at 330 lb and an inflatable cushion lift at 400 lb.

We evaluated each from listing specs and buyer feedback, not from hands-on lab work. A bath lift only works if it matches your tub, so we spend time on the measurement that decides it: the height of the tub wall compared with the lift's maximum height, and whether the suction cups can grip your tub floor.

products.name: Drive Medical Bellavita Dive Reclining Electric Bath Lift Chair
specs: Lowers to 2.6 inches from the tub bottom
products.description:
The Bellavita is the bath lift built for an actual soak. It lowers the user to within 2.6 inches of the tub bottom and raises to 18.9 inches, with a backrest that reclines 50 degrees or can be removed by a caregiver. A patented dual-column construction supports up to 310 lb through the rise and lower, and patented 3D suction feet hold the seat to the tub floor.

The controls are the most thoughtful part: large, color-coded buttons that float in the water so the user can reach them from the tub. An open seat cutout improves access for washing and hygiene. The listing gives the dimensions, 27.6 by 40.2 inches with a 15 by 20.7 inch seat and an 11.8 to 12.6 inch backrest, and notes that the lift weighs only 10.89 lb.

It sits near the top of the price range. Compared with the SuperHandy lifts it is a fixed, reclining design that does not fold, and compared with the Tranquilo it has a lower lift range. Choose it for a full, immersed bath and floating controls. Practice the lift and lower dry with the user seated and the controls in reach, and confirm the suction feet grip a clean tub floor. Dry the lift after use, charge it as the listing instructs and never use it with a damaged cord or control.
products.bestFor: Bathers who want to be lowered almost to the tub floor and recline in the water.
pros: Lowers to 2.6 inches from the tub bottom
cons: Max height of 18.9 inches may not clear a tall tub wall

products.name: Platinum Health Tranquilo Premium Electric Bath Lift with Rotating Seat
products.description:
The Tranquilo is the premium design with a padded SAFESWIVEL rotating seat, which the listing says makes transfers to and from the lift easier, more comfortable and safer. The lifting range reaches 21.5 inches, compared with 18 inches on older-style lifts, so it works with tubs that have higher sides. A heavy-duty motor and chassis carry 300 lb, and a waterproof hand controller and a lithium-ion battery with an emergency feature complete the control side.

The six-suction-cup base gives 50 percent more contact with the tub floor than older four-cup bases, and integrated transfer flaps bridge the gap between the tub ledge and the seat. An electric recline lets the user tilt the backrest once immersed. The listing urges buyers to measure the tub wall height carefully and to review the dimensions before ordering.

It sits at the top of the price range. Compared with the Bellavita it has a higher lift range and a rotating seat but a lower stated rating. Choose it for a tall tub wall or for the swivel. Read the listing's dimension notes before ordering, then practice the swivel and the lift with a helper while the tub is dry. Rinse the pads after bathing, dry the seat and keep the battery charged.
products.bestFor: Tubs with higher walls or bathers who want a swivel seat for the transfer.
pros: Six suction cups and transfer flaps

products.name: PERLECARE Electric Chair Lift for Elderly, Bath Lift for Tub, 308 lb
products.description:
The PERLECARE is a foldable electric lift with an IP68 waterproof rating and a rechargeable battery that the listing says delivers over 50 full lift-and-lower cycles per charge. The seat height runs from 2.3 to 18.9 inches, the backrest adjusts from 140 degrees to 93 degrees, and the load capacity is 308 lb on a six-point stable base that grips tile, hardwood or carpeted floors.

The quick-fold design reduces the chair to 6.4 inches in thickness, so it stores in a closet or beside furniture. An upgraded one-piece locking buckle is meant to minimize stress points and reduce breakage compared with multi-clip designs. It doubles as a floor lift for helping a user rise from the floor, and has a remote control.

It sits in the middle of the price range. Compared with the Bellavita it folds but has no floating controls or open seat. Choose it for a foldable lift that handles both the tub and the floor. Fold and unfold it a few times so the locking buckle feels familiar, and test the suction base on the tub floor before the first bath. Charge it after several uses and dry it before folding.
products.bestFor: Households that need a lift that folds and can also help from the floor.

products.name: VOCIC Electric Bath Lift for Tub AX10, 300 lb
products.description:
The VOCIC AX10 solves two practical problems: grip and moving it. It includes two types of suction cups, six of each, to match different tub and floor surfaces, anchoring to tile, polished wood, marble and smooth bathroom floors. Built-in wheels let a caregiver roll it into position beside the tub or between bathrooms. The listing describes IP68 waterproofing with a fully encased motor and sealed remote connections that allow safe submersion for about 40 minutes.

Seat height runs from 2.9 to 19.7 inches, which is the highest maximum among the electric chairs except the Tranquilo, and it folds with no assembly. The rechargeable hand control is cordless, so there is no electrical cord near water. The listing says it also helps a user rise from the floor and mentions a one-year after-sales service.

It sits in the lower-middle of the price range. Compared with the PERLECARE it has wheels and a higher maximum. Choose it for a lift you can wheel between rooms and fit to different tub surfaces. Check which of the two suction cup types grips your tub best, and test with the tub dry before the first bath. Roll it into place with the wheels, charge the remote and dry the lift before storing it.
products.bestFor: Caregivers who move the lift between rooms and need suction options for the tub.
pros: Two suction cup types, 12 in total
cons: Lower recline detail than the Bellavita

products.name: SuperHandy Portable Floor and Bath Lift, 330 lb
products.description:
The SuperHandy portable lift is the lightest powered option with a high rating. An aluminum frame weighs 19 lb, supports up to 330 lb and has a wider 23.6 by 16.1 inch base for stability. The battery-powered, IP68 design is rated for full submersion and needs no outlet near the water, and large drain holes prevent water build-up.

It folds to 28.9 by 17.7 by 4.9 inches for storage, and removable side panels allow lateral transfers to a wheelchair or bed. An arm pad adds comfort, and the listing positions it for use as both a bathtub chair lift and a floor lift to raise users from floor to standing. A wider seat with intuitive height control lets the user bathe more independently.

It sits in the middle of the price range. Compared with the electric chairs it is a more portable, panelled design. Choose it for a light, high-rated lift with transfer panels. Fold the lift for storage only when it is dry, and check the side panels lock when raised. Charge the battery regularly and wipe the arm pad and seat after use.
products.bestFor: Users who want a light, high-rated lift with side panels for lateral transfers.
cons: Max height is not given in the material we reviewed

products.name: SuperHandy Portable Inflatable Bath Lift Cushion, 400 lb
products.description:
The inflatable SuperHandy is a different kind of lift: a pneumatic cushion that inflates and deflates to raise and lower the user, with a rechargeable lithium battery and a stated 400 lb capacity. The adjustable range is 1 to 20 inches, and an integrated inflatable pillow cushions the head, neck and back.

It weighs only 15 lb and is easy to carry, move and store, and it operates quietly. Controls are built-in buttons or an infrared remote, and a full charge supports roughly 8 to 10 bathing cycles, with a low-power reminder and one or two more cycles after the warning. The inflatable design is softer than a rigid seat, though it is also less structured for transfers.

It sits in the lower-middle of the price range. Compared with the rigid chairs it is lighter and more compact but offers less rigid support. Choose it for a portable, high-rated, soft option and a quiet operation. Check the inflation and deflation cycle with the user seated, charge it after eight to ten baths and keep the cushion dry. Store it deflated, and replace it if the material is damaged.
products.bestFor: Bathers who want a quiet, portable lift and a soft backrest.
cons: Soft inflatable support is less rigid

buyingCriteria.criterion: Tub wall height against lift range
buyingCriteria.explanation: The lift has to carry the user from the tub floor up to the tub edge, so its maximum height must reach the rim. The Tranquilo reaches 21.5 inches, the VOCIC 19.7, the Bellavita and PERLECARE 18.9, and the listing for the Tranquilo warns that many lifts will not work with tall tub walls. Measure the wall from the tub floor, not from the bathroom floor, and compare. A lift that stops below the rim is a failure. Measure from the tub floor, not from the bathroom floor, and write the number down.

For a real bath, the seat needs to lower close to the tub bottom. The Bellavita goes to 2.6 inches, the PERLECARE 2.3 and the VOCIC 2.9, while the inflatable SuperHandy goes down to 1 inch. A higher minimum leaves the user with less water around their body. Consider whether a full soak matters to the user. A full soak is a comfort, and a smaller range is a safety compromise only if it still clears the rim.

A lift sits on the tub floor by suction, so the grip is everything. The Tranquilo uses six suction cups, the PERLECARE a six-point base and the VOCIC two suction cup types, six of each. Suction needs a clean, smooth tub floor, and textured or damaged surfaces reduce it. Test the lift before the user sits, and never use it on a surface that does not grip. Wipe the tub floor clean before each use, since soap film defeats suction.

The PERLECARE and VOCIC list IP68, the SuperHandy portable is IP68 and battery powered and the Bellavita has floating controls. IP68 means rated for submersion, which VOCIC specifies at about 40 minutes. Cordless, rechargeable controls avoid a mains cord near water. Charge the lift after every few uses, and know the low-battery warning. Check that any charger is kept away from water.

The Bellavita reclines 50 degrees and has an open seat, the Tranquilo has a rotating seat and electric recline, the PERLECARE backrest adjusts from 140 to 93 degrees and the SuperHandy has removable side panels. Think about how the user will get on and off the lift at tub-edge height, and which feature makes that easier. A transfer flap or rotating seat helps with the move. Practice the transfer with a helper before the first bath, with the user dry and dressed.

Ratings run from 300 lb on the Tranquilo and VOCIC to 308 on the PERLECARE, 310 on the Bellavita, 330 on the SuperHandy portable and 400 on the inflatable. Weights run from 10.89 lb on the Bellavita to 19 lb on the SuperHandy. A lift that is hard to move will stay in the tub, so think about folding and weight. If the lift needs to be moved up and down stairs, weight is also a safety factor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lift range and tub fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared maximum heights from 18.9 to 21.5 inches and minimum heights from 1 to 2.9 inches. Range was the first screen because a lift that does not reach the rim cannot work. Range was the first screen because it decides whether the lift can work at all.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at suction designs: six cups on the Tranquilo, two cup types on the VOCIC, a six-point base on the PERLECARE and the Bellavita's 3D suction feet. Suction was judged on stated design, not on promises.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water and power
howWeEvaluated.description: We read IP ratings, battery claims and control designs, including the Bellavita's floating controls and the VOCIC's cordless remote. Water ratings were read as specifications, not as guarantees.

howWeEvaluated.title: Comfort and transfer
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared recline, rotating seats, open seats and side panels. We credited features that help the user get on and off. Transfer features mattered as much as comfort.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We recorded weights and folded sizes and ratings of 300 to 400 lb, treating ratings as ceilings. Weight and folding decide whether a lift is used.

faq.q: What does a bath lift do?
faq.a: It lowers the user to near the tub bottom and raises them back to the tub edge, powered by a motor or by air. It suits people who cannot lower themselves or rise from the tub floor. It does not replace a transfer aid for getting over the tub wall.

faq.q: How do I check that it fits my tub?
faq.a: Measure the tub wall from the tub floor to the rim, and the width and length of the tub floor. Compare them to the lift's maximum height and dimensions. The Tranquilo listing warns that many lifts will not work with tall walls.
Suction works best on clean, smooth surfaces. Textured or damaged tub floors, or a non-slip mat under the lift, can reduce grip. Test the lift before the user sits, and follow the maker's guidance.
The listings give IP68 ratings or waterproof designs for bath use. VOCIC says about 40 minutes of submersion. Follow the maker's instructions, keep remotes charged and do not use a damaged unit.

faq.q: How long does the battery last?
faq.a: The PERLECARE lists over 50 cycles per charge, the inflatable SuperHandy 8 to 10 baths per charge. Charge after use and watch the low-battery reminders. Keep a charging routine.

For users with limited mobility, an occupational therapist can check that a bath lift is right, and train the user and the helper. Bring your tub measurements and the product details. They can also advise whether a lift, a bench or another aid suits the person best.

faq.q: Can a bath lift replace a transfer bench?
faq.a: No. A transfer bench helps with getting over the tub wall, while a bath lift raises and lowers the user inside the tub. Some people use both, and some lifts offer side panels or transfer flaps to help bridge the gap. If stepping over the wall is the problem, address that first.

faq.q: What should I do before the first bath?
faq.a: Practice with the tub dry and the user dressed, with a helper present. Check that the suction holds, that the controls work, that the battery is charged and that the lift reaches the tub rim. If anything feels uncertain, do not proceed until it is fixed.
